# Dialing in espresso

A standard double shot uses 18 g of ground coffee and yields about 36 g of liquid espresso. That ratio of one part coffee to two parts drink is the usual starting point for most cafes.

## How long should a shot run?

Most baristas aim for a shot time of 25 to 30 seconds. A shot that finishes in under 20 seconds usually tastes sour, while one that runs past 35 seconds tends to taste bitter and hollow. Adjust the grinder in small steps and pull a new shot after each change so you can taste the difference.

## What water temperature works best?

Brewing water between 90 and 96 °C extracts sugars and acids evenly. Lighter roasts often need the upper end of that range, around 94 °C, because their beans are denser. Darker roasts dissolve faster, so dropping the temperature by 2 °C can soften harsh notes.

## How much does a home setup cost?

A capable home grinder costs around $250, and an entry machine with a steam wand runs from $400 to $700. In a small poll of 40 home baristas, 65% said the grinder mattered more than the machine.
